messages:
alicia: Heads-up — g2-rack42-gpu07 passed the standard 24h soak but we saw 2 intermittent Xid 13s during the PCI stress window at ~23:14. Putting logs in TICKET-4821. Need a reproducible extended-soak plan before we return this node to rotation. :thinking:

ben: Can you paste the driver/kernel combo and the exact stress command? If we can repro with the same stack we can avoid a hardware RMA.

alicia: driver: nvidia-530.41.03, kernel: 6.1.0-48. Stress used: `nvme-pcie-stress` + our inferbench with sustained kv-cache churn. Command snippet attached:```
./inferbench --profile=production-heavy --batch=32 --tokens=1e6 --concurrency=4
./pci-stress --duration=3h --pattern=nvlink-flap
```

raj: Two quick theory buckets: 1) PCI enumeration flaps under nvlink stress -> driver XIDs; 2) thermal or power delivery transient causing ECC to surface as Xid. We saw similar pattern last quarter but with a different vendor card.

owen: Low-effort repro I'd try: 48h continuous inference loop + periodic `lspci -vvv` & `dmesg --follow` capture and a small PCI reset every 12h. If Xid repros shortly after reset that points to enumeration.

lin: Also add memtest (cuda-memtest) and a sustained mmap stress to rule out host-side memory corruption. Last time a host BIOS quirk surfaced only after ~36h.

alicia: Plan proposal: quarantine node -> run extended soak job on isolated rack with these phases:
- Phase A (12h): continuous inferbench (kv-cache churn) + network soak (iperf ramp)
- Phase B (24h): pci-stress w/ nvlink flapper + `lspci` snapshots every 5m + `dmesg` logging to remote collector
- Phase C (36h): thermal cycle loop (60C -> idle -> 30C) while running cuda-memtest and inferbench light
Exit criteria: no Xid >= 13 for 72h cumulative, and 0 ECC corrected/unexpected alerts beyond baseline.

ben: Sounds reasonable. Two asks: 1) automation so we can re-run on any suspect card, 2) include telemetry correlation ids so SRE console shows exact run.

sre-bot: soak-runner queued: id=soak-2245-g2-r42-07, owner=alicia, policy=extended-pci-thermal, ETA=now. Logs stream -> s3://redwood-soak/g2-rack42/gpu07/2245012345/

raj: For automation, we can reuse `soak-runner` with a new profile flag: `--profile extended-pci-thermal --retry-on-xid false --notify slack:#eng-infra`. I'll PR the profile into infra-config.

alicia: PR created: infra/soak-profiles#128 — includes exact rpm/deb pins, nvml log collectors, and a `collect-on-fail` hook to grab `/var/log/nvidia/*.log` + `pcie-logs.tar.gz`.

owen: One more: add a lightweight canary traffic replay of the actual customer workload (not just inferbench) for 6h. Higher chance of triggering cache/sequence-specific flakes.

lin: Agreed. Also capture power telemetry if possible (iDRAC/IPMI) during thermal cycling. If we see voltage droops coincident with Xid, that's telltale.

alicia: Running now. Quarantined node from pool, started soak-runner id, created hardware ticket HW-2338 for a potential follow-up RMA. Will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: soak-runner status: running -> logs: https://logs.redwood/s3/soak/g2-rack42/gpu07/2245012345/

ben: If Xid reproducible we'll try swapping PCI slot and repeating; if it moves with the card -> RMA, if it stays -> backplane/power/BIOS.

alicia: Noted. Target: finish extended plan by EOD + 24h observation. If clean -> return to rotation with `soak-pass` tag and note in node metadata. If fails -> escalate to hw-eng and schedule RMA.

raj: Thanks — appreciate the thorough plan. Keep short logs in the ticket so we can aggregate across other flakes. :eyes:
